messages:
Maya Chen: Hey team — customer reported streaming session drops + duplicate tail tokens after reconnect. They sent a pcap and say it happens consistently after ~12s of streaming.

Maya Chen: Quick summary from support: initial connect OK, stream yields ~4 chunks, client reconnects, then server resumes but last 2 tokens are duplicated and final chunk sometimes missing. Customer sees 401 on the subsequent resume attempt occasionally.

Jordan Patel: pinging eng-runtime and infra. Any quick guesses? :thinking_face:

Sarah O'Neill: My first thought — short-lived auth tokens being rotated mid-stream. If the client doesn't refresh or server rejects, you can get a forced close or 401 on the resume endpoint.

Tim Alvarez: @Maya can you paste the pcap link and the Request-IDs from the logs?

Maya Chen: pcap uploaded: https://pcap-storage.internal/streams/1864567890.pcap (pcap-bot attached). Logs show request_id=rid_09f4a2 and stream_id=s_1ab3c. I'm dropping a snippet of the streaming request headers from customer logs: 

```
GET /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.bio
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-temp-XXXX
Accept: text/event-stream
X-Stream-Id: s_1ab3c
```

Maya Chen: After about 12s there's a TLS close, then client reconnects with a new Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-temp-YYYY and does an SSE resume call `POST /v1/streams/s_resume`. Sometimes server returns 200 and resumes, sometimes 401.

Jordan Patel: Can we see the server trace for rid_09f4a2? I want to know whether the server forced close or if the client RSTed.

pcap-bot: pcap analysis: TCP session shows FIN from client at 12.034s, then SYN/ACK and new handshake. No obvious RST. TLS close_notify present. Reconstructed SSE frames show partial last event: `data: "...the result stop"

` (no trailing newline).

Sarah O'Neill: Partial final event with no terminating newline can make some clients treat it as incomplete and then the client will re-request resume. That can explain duplicated tokens if the server resends last partial chunk.

Tim Alvarez: Also check keepalive/idle timeouts on LB/nginx. If ingress closes idle https connections at 10s, it can cut the stream leading to a client-initiated reconnect. @ingress-bot any recent config changes?

ingress-bot: No config changes in the last 30d on streaming ELB idle timeout (still 60s). However the path health check show occasional 504s to the streaming shard around the same timeframe.

Jordan Patel: Hmm. Two likely failure modes in-stack: token TTL too short causing 401 on resume, or client-side conservative idle detection causing FIN after not seeing a final newline + heartbeat.

Maya Chen: Customer says tokens are minted with 15s TTL for ephemeral demo flows — that'll bite streaming.

Sarah O'Neill: Yeah streaming requires longer-lived session tokens or a refresh mechanism that doesn't re-auth the resumed stream as a new session. For hosted API we recommend >= 5min for streaming tokens or use refresh tokens on the client to re-auth transparently.

Maya Chen: Repro steps I used locally: 
1) Start a server with a short token TTL (15s).
2) curl SSE with `--no-buffer` and stream a payload that yields chunks over 30s.
3) Force a client reconnect after 12s.

Example curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-temp-AAA" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  "https://api.redwood.bio/v1/streams/generate?model=small"
```

Jordan Patel: Can you also try with the python SSE client? Some clients auto-combine events and hide newline issues.

Maya Chen: done. Python sseclient yields same behavior when token TTL is short. When I bumped TTL to 10m the resume always returns 200 and no duplicates.

Tim Alvarez: Good repro. Next steps: 1) Tell customer to extend stream token TTL for their production usage (or implement refresh flow). 2) We should add server-side guard: when resuming, dedupe last N tokens by sequence id if available. 3) Add a small heartbeat event every 5s to avoid client idle heuristics. 4) Engineering to check why partial event lacks newline — investigate encoder flush at end-of-chunk.

Sarah O'Neill: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket for the dedupe logic + flush fix. Can someone attach logs (rid_09f4a2) and the trace id?

Maya Chen: Logs attached in thread. Server trace: trace_id=tr_77b4c. Key log lines: 
```
[10:23:11.234] stream_start rid_09f4a2 s_1ab3c
[10:23:23.268] chunk_sent seq=34 stream_id=s_1ab3c
[10:23:23.268] connection_close remote=client FIN
[10:23:23.300] resume_request rid_09f4a2-resume token=sk-prod-temp-YYYY -> 200 OR 401 (race)
[10:23:23.350] send_resume_payload seq=35 seq_dup_check_miss
```

Tim Alvarez: The `seq_dup_check_miss` means resume path didn't have the previous sequence window persisted. Maybe an in-memory session expired because TTL was keyed to token lifetime. We'll want to separate session window lifetime from token TTL.

Jordan Patel: Agreed. For now propose immediate customer mitigation: extend TTL to 5–10min or switch to long-lived session tokens for streaming. Also suggest adding `retry: 1000` SSE and an explicit `id:` field per event so clients can resume reliably.

Maya Chen: I sent that recommendation. Customer is ok to try a TTL increase.

Sarah O'Neill: Ops/Infra: can we surface a streaming-specific metric that counts resume-401s and resume-duplicates per model/shard? That'd help detect this class of bug.

Tim Alvarez: I'll add a Grafana panel and alert for resume_401_rate > 0.1% of resumes. Also add a short-term log extractor to correlate resume requests with token issue times.

pcap-bot: Additional pcap note: client includes TCP keepalive, but application-layer heartbeat missing. In some reconnections there's a 1–2s gap during TLS negotiation which is fine, but client treats that as a hard close because final newline never arrived.

Jordan Patel: Summary action list: 
- Support: advise customer to extend token TTL and test. (Maya)
- Eng-runtime: add dedupe-on-resume, ensure sequence window persists beyond token TTL, flush final newline on chunk completion. (Sarah)
- Infra: add resume_401/duplicate metrics + Grafana + alert. (Tim)
- Devex/docs: publish best-practices for streaming tokens + SSE id/retry examples. (Jordan)

Maya Chen: Marking as high priority customer escalation. I'll update customer once TTL test completes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Tim Alvarez: tagging eng-runtime with trace_id=tr_77b4c and pcap link.

Jordan Patel: If customer still sees duplicates after TTL bump, we'll need pcap + full heap of server side session state for the window around seq=34.

Maya Chen: will request and post. Closing interim triage.
